# Ingot

Ingot is a Bittensor subnet. A fixed open-source teacher model in BF16 is the reference.
Miners submit quantized copies of it with the same architecture, no larger than genesis. The
validator measures how far each copy drifts from the teacher, token by token and layer by layer,
and crowns the copy that beats the current king by a margin.

The subnet runs one quantization at a time, the open one (`chain.toml` `[competition]
active_quant`). Each quantization has its own genesis, its own rules and its own line of kings,
mirrored to Hugging Face under https://huggingface.co/dendriteholdings as
`Ingot-<roman numeral>-<king_name>`, numbered per quantization: `27B-Q2` today, `27B-FP8` before
it. The newest five kings of any quantization share the emission for five days each; the rest
burns to uid 0.

The model to beat is always the newest king of the open quantization. Before its first
coronation it is that quantization's genesis.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Teacher | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (BF16) |
| Open quantization | `qwen38_27b:q2`: ternary, one GGUF file |
| q2 genesis | `dendriteholdings/Ingot-genesis-27B-Q2`, file `Ingot-genesis-27B-Q2.gguf` (7,206,168,928 bytes; `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PQ2_0.gguf` of `prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf`, unchanged) |
| q2 runtime | the PrismML llama.cpp fork at `e3de715` (tag `prism-b10777-e3de715`), the `llama-prism` submodule |
| Closed | `qwen38_27b:fp8`, genesis `dendriteholdings/Ingot-genesis-27B-FP8` (rules kept below) |
| Source of truth | `chain.toml` in this repo |

## What a q2 submission must be

The rule in one line: **the genesis GGUF file with your own weight values.** Everything except
the weight bytes is genesis's, compared against genesis's header pinned in the repo
(`src/model_validation/families/qwen38_27b/genesis_q2.json`).

- **One file.** Exactly one `*.gguf` at the top level (any name not starting with `.`), nothing
  else: no tokenizer, README, `config.json`, `mmproj` or split GGUF. At most 8,000,000,000 bytes
  uploaded, and the file at most 7,206,168,928 bytes, genesis's size.
- **A clean container,** read by our own strict parser: GGUF v3; no duplicate keys or tensors;
  tensors aligned and packed back to back with zero padding; each tensor exactly the bytes its
  type and shape need; nothing after the last tensor.
- **Genesis's metadata, all of it.** Every key with the same type and value, no key added: the
  `qwen35` architecture, the tokenizer and chat template, and the `prism.hadamard.*` rotation
  (which weights are stored rotated, block size, signs).
- **Genesis's tensors.** The same 851 names and shapes, nothing added or missing. A tensor genesis
  keeps unquantized (F32/BF16: norms, `ssm_a`, `ssm_conv1d`, `ssm_dt`, `ssm_norm`,
  `ssm_alpha`, `ssm_beta`) keeps its type. A tensor genesis stores as PQ2_0 may use any accepted
  type (PQ2_0, Q8_0, F16, BF16, F32), but at genesis's size no wider type fits, so in practice
  every one stays PQ2_0.
- **Ternary.** PQ2_0 stores each weight as a 2-bit code times its block's fp16 scale (128
  weights per block); the codes are −1, 0 and +1. The fourth code (`11`, which the fork decodes as
  +2) rejects the model.
- **Sane values.** Every value is finite (no NaN, no infinity), and every weight is at most
  10,000 in size once dequantized (a block's |scale| × its largest code, or a F32/F16/BF16 value
  itself). Genesis peaks at 0.44 and 139; the cap only stops values the fork's fp16 paths would
  overflow on.

Your weight values are yours: retrain the ternary codes, re-fit the scales, tune the norm gains
and the other unquantized values, fine-tune or distill from the teacher.

`ingot check-model --path ./model.gguf` (or `scripts/validate_model.py --path ./model.gguf`) runs
every check locally and prints each one.

## What an fp8 submission must be (closed)

- The genesis model: `config.json` equals genesis on every value except the free keys
  (`quantization_config.weight_block_size`, `quantization_config.modules_to_not_convert`,
  `transformers_version`, `use_cache`, `initializer_range`, `attention_dropout`), and holds no
  key genesis does not. `quant_method` is `fp8`.
- The genesis tensors: every weight of `dendriteholdings/Ingot-genesis-27B-FP8` keeps its name and
  shape, nothing is added; scale tensors are not compared to genesis, they follow your block size.
  In the text model a weight may be BF16 or F32, or FP8 E4M3 where genesis has it in FP8: vLLM
  serves nothing else quantized (an FP8 `embed_tokens` does not load). The projections vLLM fuses
  into one layer (`q/k/v_proj`, `gate/up_proj`, `in_proj_qkv/in_proj_z`, `in_proj_b/in_proj_a`)
  are all FP8 or all unquantized. Tensors under `model.visual.`, `mtp.` and `lm_head.` keep the
  genesis dtype (`lm_head` stays BF16: the evaluator applies it itself to your last hidden
  state). An FP8 weight `x.weight` carries `x.weight_scale_inv` shaped by your
  `weight_block_size` (two ints, 128 or larger), and `modules_to_not_convert` lists every 2-D
  weight you left unquantized, in the text model and the vision tower alike; the embeddings and
  `lm_head` aside, which vLLM never quantizes, and norms and biases, which need no entry. vLLM
  builds an unlisted one as FP8 and does not load. Every value is finite.
- No larger than genesis: the tensors outside `model.visual.` and `mtp.` together hold at most
  29,468,003,328 bytes, genesis's text model.
- Exactly these files, all at the top level: `config.json`, `model.safetensors.index.json` and
  the `*.safetensors` shards the index names (names are free). Every tensor is in exactly one
  shard, the one the index names. Any other file rejects the submission; a king is published
  with genesis's tokenizer and license added.

A rejected submission shows its reason in the status the validator publishes (below).

## Your own quantization, not someone else's

Before the evaluation the validator fingerprints your weights: what is left of them once every
rearrangement that leaves the model's output unchanged is undone (permuted or rescaled
neurons, heads and channels, moved norm gains, a permuted, rotated or rescaled residual stream)
is your quantization error against the teacher. A q2 model is read exactly as the fork runs it,
dequantized and taken out of its Hadamard rotation, and compared with the same BF16 teacher.
Independent quantizations make unrelated errors. The fingerprint is compared with that
quantization's genesis and with every earlier submission of other miners of the same
quantization that passed this check; your own earlier models (same hotkey or coldkey) are never
held against you.

A submission is rejected as a duplicate, and its hotkey is spent, only when it is the same
model as such a one: identical tensors, an error correlating with that model's at `COPY_CORR`
(0.9999) or more over the whole model, or tensors holding `COPIED_FRAC` (99%) of its error each
correlating at `PART_CORR` (0.9999) or more (`src/model_dedup/config.py`). A model you trained
on from a king is yours: its error is still mostly the king's (a fine-tune moves it by a few
percent, a correlation of about 0.999) and it passes; the eval then holds it to the same bar as
any model, the margin over the current king. The same deterministic recipe run on the same data
gives the same model: if someone submitted it first, yours is the duplicate. Re-uploading a king
with a little noise does not pay: it passes this check and loses its duel.

## How a submission is judged

The evaluation dataset is the Hugging Face Parquet dataset and split named in `chain.toml`
`[dataset]`. The evaluator draws `SAMPLES_PER_DOMAIN` (40) prompts from every domain and
`DOMAIN_SAMPLES` (150) from each agent domain, swe and terminal, seeded by the block hash of your
`r2ready` commitment. Inside a domain it spreads the draw as evenly as possible over the languages
available there, then picks rows at random from each language; the seed makes the same draw
reproducible on every validator (`eval_service/dataset.py`). An agent domain's row is an agent's
conversation cut before one of its turns: the task, the tool schemas, and the agent's earlier tool
calls and their output, up to `MAX_MODEL_LEN` (65536) tokens with the answer. The teacher answers
each prompt in vLLM (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, at most `MAX_TOKENS` tokens); the
king and your model then read exactly the teacher's prompt and answer. Only the answer tokens are
scored. For each model, per answer token:

- KL: KL(teacher ‖ model) between the next-token distributions.
- Distance: |h_model − h_teacher| / |h_teacher|, the hidden state's distance from the teacher's
  as a fraction of the teacher's length, averaged over the layers in `LAYERS`.

Lower is better. The teacher rereading its own answer gives the noise floor, recorded with
every eval: batching alone makes two runs of the same model differ by about that much.

Every eval runs on one machine, the eval box: eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition
GPUs (96 GB each, driver 595.84, CUDA 13.2), two Xeon Platinum 8563C (104 cores) and 1 TB of RAM,
Ubuntu 24.04. Four GPUs serve the teacher in vLLM; the king reads on two and the challenger
on the other two. The fork is built on that box (`scripts/build_llama.sh`)
with CUDA 13.0 and GCC 13.3, its kernels for `sm_120a` only: a q2 model is read with the fork's
PQ2_0 CUDA kernels as they compile for Blackwell.

**q2 (GGUF)** models read the answer in `llama-states` (`src/eval_service/llama_states/`), a
small program on the pinned fork's own library, `LLAMA_PER_GPU` (4) processes on the model's
GPU, each one request at a time, flash attention, a 16-bit KV cache, passes of 2048 tokens, the
hidden states after every 8th block taken by the fork's own layer capture. The evaluator rebuilds
the next-token distribution from your last hidden state with your own `output_norm` and
`output.weight`, dequantized exactly and with the fork's Hadamard rotation applied, in float32
(`GgufHead`, `src/eval_service/metrics.py`); checked against the fork's own logits, the two agree
to a KL of 0.000005. Run under the fork, the teacher itself lands at a KL of 0.00007 from the
vLLM teacher: the engine difference is far below the margins.

**fp8** models read it in vLLM 0.31.0, one server per GPU: `--language-model-only
--max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 65536 --no-enable-chunked-prefill
--no-enable-prefix-caching --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 --gdn-prefill-backend triton`, plus a
logits processor that forces the teacher's tokens and hidden-state extraction at `LAYERS`
(`src/eval_service/servers.py`). The evaluator applies the final norm (float32) and `lm_head`
(BF16 weights, logits kept in float32) itself from your own tensors.

You win if your KL is lower than the king's by at least `KL_MARGIN` (1.5%) of the king's KL, and
your distance lower than the king's by at least `DIST_MARGIN` (0.84%) of the king's distance, both
measured in the same eval: both, so a large gain on one cannot make up for a loss on the other.
The margins are shares of the king's score, so the absolute bar shrinks as kings near the teacher.
The margins, the sample counts and the layers are in `src/eval_service/config.py`. A win makes
you the new king immediately; a loss is final for that hotkey.

A model that diverges loses: one that leaves the teacher's answer while reading it, or whose score
comes out NaN or infinite on any sample. A diverged king loses to any challenger that did not
diverge. A model that fails to load or stops responding during the eval is "the model does not
run"; when it is the king's that fails, the challenger is queued again without losing an attempt.

## Who gets paid

`src/common/reign.py`: the newest `SLOTS` (5) kings, of any quantization, each receive
`SHARE` (0.2) of the emission for `REIGN_DAYS` (5) after their coronation. A king stops earning
when its reign is over or when five newer kings exist, whichever comes first. Whatever is not
assigned goes to uid 0. One king: 20% to it, 80% burned. Five fresh kings: 20% each. Only the
open quantization crowns new kings; a closed one's kings earn out their reign.

A king whose uid is re-registered by another hotkey loses its share.

## Hotkeys

- One submission per hotkey. Once a model is evaluated, win or lose, the hotkey is spent.
- A submission that fails validation hands the upload attempt back; up to
  `MAX_UPLOAD_ATTEMPTS` (3) per hotkey (`src/chain_reader/config.py`).
- A submission rejected as a duplicate spends the hotkey; no attempt is handed back.
- A hotkey swap (same uid, same registration block, new hotkey) bars the new hotkey.
- Identical model bytes cannot be in the pipeline twice. A digest held by a submission that
  failed (INVALID, FAILED) is free again.
- If the open quantization changes while your submission waits, it ends FAILED with "closed":
  no strike against your hotkey, and you get an extra attempt for the open one.

## Submitting a model

Your model never goes to a public URL. It is uploaded to the subnet's private bucket and only
becomes public if it wins.

1. `r2activate:v2:<family>:<quant>:<base64url pubkey>` — you declare the model family and
   quantization you upload: a pair listed in `chain.toml` `[quants]`, and only the open one
   (`qwen38_27b:q2` today) gets credentials. The CLI takes `--family` / `--quant`, defaulting to
   the open pair. It generates a one-time Ed25519 key and commits its public half on chain. Your
   upload limit and the validation rules are those of the declared pair. The validator mints
   storage credentials scoped to your own folder, encrypts them to that key and publishes them in
   a public mailbox.
2. The CLI decrypts the credentials and uploads the model files (for q2, `--path` may be the
   `.gguf` file itself).
3. `r2ready:v2:<model digest>` — freezes the upload. The digest is one sha256 over every file's
   path, size and sha256. The validator revokes the credentials, checks the file names and the
   upload limit, re-hashes every byte against the digest when it downloads the model, and
   queues the submission for validation and evaluation.

Budgets: `UPLOAD_WINDOW_S` (24 h) from activate to ready; an upload is at most the
`upload_limit` of the pair you declared (8 GB for `qwen38_27b.q2`, 35 GB for `qwen38_27b.fp8`);
going over it closes the upload and deletes it; bytes are kept `RETENTION_HOURS` (72) after they
are no longer needed. Your status, including attempts left and the reason for any rejection, is
published as plaintext at `<mailbox_url>/mailbox/v1/<registration_id>/status.json`; the CLI reads
it for you.

Local state lives in `./.ingot-miner/<hotkey>/`: `submission-key` must survive from
activate to ready on the same machine; `upload-auth.json` is removed at ready.

## A q2 king

A crowned q2 king is published as `Ingot-<N>-27B-Q2` with its file renamed
`Ingot-<N>-27B-Q2.gguf`, genesis's `LICENSE` and `NOTICE.txt`, and a card with its winning
duel's scores, its gain over genesis, and how to run it: the fork at the commit Ingot scored it
with (`llama-server -m Ingot-<N>-27B-Q2.gguf -ngl 99 -fa on --jinja`), and genesis's vision
projector from `prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf` (`--mmproj Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-mmproj-Q8_0.gguf`) for image input, which Ingot does not
score.

## The CLI

```
uv sync && cp .env.example_miners .env         # INGOT_COLDKEY, INGOT_HOTKEY, netuid, network
uv run ingot register                          # burned registration
uv run ingot check-model --path ./model.gguf
uv run ingot submit-private --path ./model.gguf  # activate → upload → ready
uv run ingot activate                          # the same, one step at a time
uv run ingot upload-private --path ./model.gguf
uv run ingot ready --model-digest <hash>
```

Every flag defaults to the matching `INGOT_*` value in `.env`. `--yes` skips the confirm
prompts. The mailbox URL, the chain generation and the open pair come from `chain.toml`; nothing
else needs configuring. To run a model as the eval does, build the fork pinned in `llama-prism`
(`bash scripts/build_llama.sh`).
